title: Onboarding IO fingerprint and performance artifact specification
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Define a stable, machine-readable IO fingerprint and a companion performance artifact to be published with every onboarded model. The IO fingerprint captures canonical prompt serialization, supported parameter names and aliases, enforced response envelope schema, and metadata keys (e.g., model_commit, quantization, tokenizer_version). The performance artifact (perf-profile) provides p50/p95 latency envelopes, tokens-per-second throughput targeting typical batch sizes, estimated cost-per-1k-tokens, and a simple regression vector for key prompt sets.

Goal: give downstream engineers a signed contract that their prompts and routing policies can depend on, plus enough perf telemetry to make routing/cost choices. The artifact should be verifiable by the runtime during model load and by CI jobs during canary deploys.

Scope: onboarding new open and internal models used by hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This ticket specifies artifact formats, publishing workflow, CI gating rules, and the runtime validation hooks. It does not implement the full console UI (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: A stable JSON schema for io-fingerprint is published (io-fingerprint-v1.schema.json) and stored in the model-catalog; schema includes: prompt_serialization, parameter_map, response_envelope, metadata_keys, compatibility_level.
A perf-profile format (perf-profile-v1.json) is defined and includes: latency_percentiles, throughput_by_batch, token_cost_estimate, benchmark_prompt_set_ids.
Onboard CLI generates the two artifacts and signs them with the org KMS, producing model-catalog entries that the runtime can fetch.
Runtime implements a lightweight verification that rejects model loads where the declared tokenizer_version or required metadata_keys are missing unless compatibility_level permits fallback.
CI gating job (onboard-check) runs on PRs that change the artifacts and fails if golden-output diffs exceed thresholds or p95 latency regresses > 15%.
Developer docs and a short example showing how to write a semantic alias mapping for parameter names are published in Confluence links provided below.
proposal:
1) IO fingerprint: canonicalize prompt serialization as 'prompt_v1' — a compact JSONL with explicit message roles, length-limited context markers, and normalized tokens_to_return field. Provide a parameter_map that lists primary names and aliases (e.g., 'max_tokens': ['max_tokens','max_tokens_limit','maxTokens']). Include compatibility_level: 'strict'|'stable'|'relaxed' to indicate acceptable server-side aliasing/duck-typing.

2) Perf-profile: run a fixed harness (bench/standard) producing p50/p95 latency for sequence lengths {64,256,1024} and batch sizes {1,4,8}. Publish throughput_by_batch and cost_estimate per 1k tokens under a named hardware profile (e.g., A100-40GB-onnx). Attach benchmark_prompt_set_ids referencing canonical eval prompts stored in the model-catalog.

3) Signing & Registry: artifacts bundled into a tarball <model>-artifacts-v1.tar.gz with SHA256 signed by KMS. The model-catalog stores artifact URLs, signature, and short human-readable summary.

4) Runtime & CI: runtime validates presence and signature of artifacts during model load and emits a compatibility badge. CI runs onboard-check which (a) runs golden prompts and compares normalized outputs (token-level and semantic hashes), (b) runs the perf harness and compares latency envelopes with adaptive thresholds. Failures block canary rollout.

5) Compatibility tiers: Strict = exact envelope/param names; Stable = allowed aliases and deterministic shape; Relaxed = best-effort mapping and behavioral heuristics.
implementation_notes: Add onboarding-cli command: `redwood onboard --emit-artifacts` that produces io-fingerprint-v1.json and perf-profile-v1.json and requests KMS signature.
Model-catalog metadata fields: artifact_urls, artifact_signature, artifact_schema_version, hardware_profile, benchmark_prompt_set_ids.
Runtime hook: model_loader.verify_artifacts(model_id) -> warning/fail depending on compatibility_level and missing keys.
CI job: .github/workflows/onboard-check.yml uses an ephemeral cluster, runs bench/standard against candidate model, compares outputs using semantic-hash and token-diff thresholds.
Console: surface compatibility_level and perf-profile summary tile (follow-up UI ticket).
test_plan: Golden-output regression tests: compare candidate outputs to golden for the canonical prompt set using a two-tier diff (token-diff % and semantic-hash).
Parameter aliasing fuzz: generate variations of parameter names and ensure alias mapping resolves to canonical names according to parameter_map.
Latency envelope verification: run bench/standard at sequence lengths 64/256/1024 and batch sizes 1/4/8 and assert p95 within allowed delta vs published perf-profile.
Quantization mismatch test: validate that declared quantization in metadata matches actual runtime execution path; if mismatch, annotate compatibility_level with 'quantization_mismatch'.
Upgrade path tests: simulate model update with minor I/O changes and verify that 'stable' tier allows rollout while 'strict' blocks.
updates: 2025-02-01: Ticket created by Maya to capture spec work for model artifacts.
2025-02-03: Scoping meeting with runtime, infra, and QA — agreed on three compatibility tiers and KMS signing.
2025-02-06: Drafted io-fingerprint schema and perf-profile fields; pushed initial draft to Confluence.
2025-02-09: Design review with Asha and Lin — feedback to add benchmark_prompt_set_ids and explicit hardware_profile in perf-profile.
2025-02-12: Rafael volunteered to implement onboarding-cli plumbing; Rafael flagged existing dependency on infra KMS onboarding (follow-up: ENG-44501).
decision: Adopt v1 artifact formats (io-fingerprint-v1, perf-profile-v1), sign artifacts with org KMS, implement runtime verification and CI gating. Use three compatibility tiers and publish the artifacts in the model-catalog. Console UI to follow in separate ticket.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land schema + onboarding-cli and CI job in a feature branch and run against 3 internal models. Phase 2: enable runtime verification in non-blocking mode for 2 weeks, emit warnings. Phase 3: switch CI to blocking mode and enable runtime strict validation for a small subset of customer-facing deployments. Communicate to partners and include migration doc for previously onboarded models.
